confidence_note: From memory and secondary knowledge; book text not accessed. Finland half marathon barefoot in shorts, about -20 C, is a well-documented Hof feat; the old TR text said Arctic marathon, which is wrong. Radboud University endotoxin study: 24 healthy young men, 12 trained for 10 days, fewer flu-like symptoms, higher adrenaline and anti-inflammatory response; recalled from published research, whether the book describes it exactly is unverified. Three pillars (breathing, cold, commitment) recalled; old TR said meditation. Old claims (ancestors, 'doctors said hypothermia inevitable', Hof himself injected) dropped. Small sample caveat added in the story. DB title is Turkish 'Soguk Yontem'; English title assumed.
facts: Hof ran a half marathon barefoot in shorts above the Arctic Circle in Finland at about -20 C.
He teaches that such feats are learnable.
Three pillars: breathing, cold exposure, commitment.
Breathing: deliberate deep breaths followed by breath-holding.
Radboud University study: 24 healthy young men injected with bacterial endotoxin.
Twelve trained ten days; twelve did not.
Trained group reported fewer flu-like symptoms, higher adrenaline and anti-inflammatory response.
Small sample; does not show anyone can match Hof.
tension: A dramatic feat versus a small study.
reflect_final: Which claim you recently believed rested on a striking story rather than on anything you could check yourself?

use_cases.move: Look up the research and ask a doctor.

pocket_idea: Hof's barefoot run and a 24-person study are different evidence.

conversation_variants.punchline_idea: A barefoot run and a 24-person study are different kinds of evidence.
